naics_industry_sector: Manufacturing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used for BSA Seafood, LLC of Grasonville, Maryland to purchase and install equipment at the newly purchased facility located at 75 Engerman, Denton, Maryland. This expansion site will be used to purchase invasive blue catfish from regional watermen, process and produce value-added product and distribute directly to restaurants, retailers, cash-and-carry, and institutions. By targeting MPPEP funds to equipment, minimal installation, and launch staffing, this project resolves the core processing constraints in our geography, increases annual removals of invasive blue catfish, unlocks value-added markets, expands commercial outlets for fishers, and delivers measurable outcomes: over 500,000 pounds per year processed, four new products (six total), at least ten additional producers served, thirty new sales placements, and 20 Full time jobs created with 15 retained.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to extend sanitary sewer service to the area of Lewis Road in rural Berlin, Maryland, located in Worcester County. The project will be an extension of the existing "Landings" sewer service area. Both residents and the environment will benefit as the proposed project will alleviate the health and sanitary problems currently caused by failing septic systems. The proposed project will consist of constructing a gravity sewer collection system with a central grinder pump station to connect 46 residential and 3 commercial users to the existing Landings WWTP. Approximately 116 residents are expected to benefit from this project, which meets Rural Developments goal of serving a targeted area.

The Farm to Freezer Facility aims to solve a number of problems in the region, including increasing the availability of locally processed produce, especially to areas of the Eastern Shore having limited access; creating increased revenue and profit margin opportunities for local farmers and growers by providing wider access to different markets; and creating the opportunity for growers to scale and diversify their production and increase employment. The facility will occupy 5,000 square feet, with half the space used for processing and Individual Quick Frozen equipment and the other half set aside for refrigerated, freezer, and dry storage and staging for shipping and receiving. The community served by this project includes several counties on the Eastern Shore Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Annes, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester where the estimated poverty rate is over 13 percent and access to nutritious food is limited.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to support Westminster Rescue Missions Addiction Healing Center (AHC) and better prepare and equip the staff and facility to handle the COVID-19 pandemic. This support includes broadened access to COVID-19 testing and vaccination, better preparation for an influx of individuals seeking Substance Use Disorder Treatment, and better support for the AHC clients. With COVID-19 playing a huge part in the opioid crisis, AHC is providing double the treatment, leading to the need for additional staffing. The center plans to hire a nurse practitioner, peer recovery coordinator, and client care coordinator. Drug and alcohol use has increased during the pandemic, but the number of people seeking treatment decreased with the fear of exposure to COVID-19. WRM will be able to treat these patients in all areas with the additional staff to support the ongoing efforts to combat this pandemic.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase an ambulance for Pocomoke City that will improve access to emergency medical services during the surge of the COVID-19 pandemic. This new ambulance will replace an older vehicle that is lacking many safety and health standards critical to COVID safety, including better air filtration with heating, ventilation and air conditioning comprehensive air disinfection, and a power lift system for administering oxygen. The need to increase safety during medical emergencies is especially important to the vulnerable populations of Pocomoke City. As of the 2019 Census, data shows that Pocomoke City is comprised of nearly 51 percent minority populations, and approximately 22 percent of the population is living in poverty. These features are not only important to the patients, but also to the crew maneuvering the equipment. Pocomoke City reported that more than 50% of their EMS personnel contracted COVID over the last two years. With these factors in mind, this funding is imperative to the health and safety of Pocomoke City.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to replace a portion of the ductile iron pipe and fittings which have deteriorated as a result of the acidity level of the soils. This line connects the county water district to the city of Frostburgs system, the water supplier, at State Route 55. Due to the acidic soils in the area, the water district has been losing approximately 25 percent of its purchased water for several years due to line leaks and breakages. Once completed, the improvements will reduce breaks, leaks, and ultimately the amount of lost water in the system. This is a water service to approximately 100 homes and currently provides an emergency connection to the town of Lonaconings water distribution system in Midland, Maryland.

This increase to 2,300 customers per year (4,050 over the two year grant period) will be the result of enhancing the labelling (to market as local and free range) and promoting the farms eggs to the local market through advertising and agritourism channels.

funding_code: (COMB LOAN & GRANT) WATER ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to fund construction upgrades to the Town of Lonaconings water system. The upgrades will include rehabilitation and expansion of the Koontz Water Treatment Plant, the Gilmore Water Treatment Plant, dam reservoir repairs to the Midland-Gilmore Dam, and waterline replacement to the Pekin-Moscow service area. The water treatment plants have operated since 1989 and have reached the end of their service life. Marylands Dam Safety Divisions recent inspection deemed the reservoir unsafe. The waterline had experienced a break in December 2018, disabling residents access to water for three days. This investment is needed for Lonaconing to meet health and sanitary standards. This project, fully funded by a partnership with the state of Maryland, will serve 2,357 people.

project_name: North Branch Sewage Pumping Station Upgrade
funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) WASTE DISPOSAL ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to fund the construction of the Countys North Branch Pump Station. The original funding for the project consisted of an ARC Grant in the amount of $700,000.00; RUS Direct Loan of $1,092,000.00 and Applicant Funds of $118,000.00; which were obligated in September 2018. However, bids were received higher than the engineers original estimate, thus the need for the additional RUS Grant funding. The North Branch Pump Station is located outside of the City of Cumberland, near Mexico Farms service area, which is a heavy industrial area which offers employment to the area. The upgrade will replace outdated equipment with high energy efficient motors on pumps and blowers. The existing pump station has had no major improvements since its original construction over 25 years ago. This pump station serves 153 residential users and 5 large industrial users that produce large flows and its efficient and functional operations are critical to the users.

program: SEARCH - Special Evaluation Assistance for Rural Communities and Households Grant (WEP)
funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) SEARCH GRANTS WATER ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to assist with the costs associated with the preparation of a Preliminary Engineering Report and an Environmental Report for the towns water system. The systems water distribution lines are nearing 100 years in age and there is evidence of excessive amounts of water loss due to the deteriorated condition of these pipes. Due to the excessive and severe breaks in the lines the water quality is impacted and exposed pipes are a potential health and safety hazard to the public. The report will evaluate the existing system and determine the best alternative to repair, upgrade or replace elements of the system to better ensure the delivery of safe, reliable drinking water to the town and its residents.

naics_industry_sector: Other or Not Defined
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase a refrigerated van to transport meals to needy children and seniors. During the Covid-19 pandemic, Friends of the Grape, through Caroline County Public Schools, and in partnership with other local government agencies, has been feeding and transporting meals to 1200 students and 300 senior citizens per day. The targeted delivery area at this time is the Marydel, Templeville, and Henderson areas that have high poverty and minority populations. This area has been identified as a Food Desert by Johns Hopkins. Currently 15,000 nutritious meals per week are delivered to these three areas of Caroline County, and the route takes 3-4 hours each day to complete. The refrigerated van will allow food to be held at proper temperatures, in order to minimize the risk a food borne illness, and will allow for further outreach of service.

funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) PRE-DEVELOPMENT GRANTS - WASTE ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will assist with costs associated with preparing a preliminary engineering and environmental report for the Town of Hancocks sanitary sewer system. The Town is currently operating under a Consent Order issued by the Maryland Department of the Environment for ongoing effluent ammonia violations. The current system is outdated. Additionally, there are known I&I issues in the system, and there have been extensive repairs with the existing four (4) pump houses. The funding will enable the Town to fully evaluate alternatives in recommending upgrades to their existing Wastewater Treatment Plant and collection system to bring their sanitary sewer system within compliance.

program: SEARCH - Special Evaluation Assistance for Rural Communities and Households Grant (WEP)
funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) SEARCH GRANTS WATER ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will assist with costs associated with the preparation of a Preliminary Engineering Report and an Environmental Report for The Town of Hancocks water system. The systems distribution lines are nearly a century old, and its cast-iron water mains are corroded and rusted. Constant and ineffective repairs of breaks and leaks have unnecessarily consumed the towns labor and time. Only one operational drinking well and a three day supply of drinking water remain on hand. If the well becomes inoperable, the town will lose fresh drinking water access. The Preliminary Engineering Report and the Environmental Report will evaluate the existing system and determine the best alternative to repair, upgrade, or replace the systems elements.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to for the expansion of rural learning programs that provide educational instruction and job training related to potential employment or job advancements for adult students. The purpose of this funding program is to support targeted technical assistance, training, and other activities leading to the development or expansion of small and emerging private businesses in rural areas. Carroll Community College Foundation received a USDA Rural Business Development Grant in 2017 to purchase educational equipment for their Emergency Medical Services program.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to assist with the preparation of a preliminary engineering and environmental report for the town of Emmitsburgs existing pump station. The town has been experiencing large Sanitary Sewer Overflows (SSOs) during the past two years, as documented by the Maryland Department of the Environment, and engineers have contributed the overflows to the existing pump station, which is at the end of its useful life. More than 68,000-gallons of SSOs have flooded the nearby Flat Run Creek. This funding will assist the town with the preparation of the reports to fully evaluate alternatives to recommend either an upgrade to their existing pump station or a replacement to bring their sanitary sewer system in compliance with the states environmental requirements.

funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) PRE-DEVELOPMENT GRANTS - WASTE ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to fund a Preliminary Engineering Report (PER) and an Environmental Report (ER) for the wastewater treatment plant in the town of Pittsville located in Wicomico County, Maryland. The reports will provide an analysis of the project alternatives and estimated costs to improve the operation of the municipal wastewater treatment plant. The PER and ER will draw conclusions on whether the proposed project is feasible and will or will not have environmental impacts.

funding_code: RBCS ENTERPRISE GRANTS
naics_industry_sector: Public Administration
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide technical assistance to small and emerging businesses. Pocomoke City will hire a consultant to develop and implement a marketing campaign to promote their downtown businesses. The project will be used for various marketing aspects of the campaign and activities will compliment other downtown incentives and improvements the city has implemented.

funding_code: VALUE-ADDED PRODUCER DVLP GRANTS-DISCR
naics_industry_sector: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used by Chesapeake Bay Dairy, LLC to produce sour cream, yogurt, and Greek-style yogurt on their dairy farm in Pocomoke City (Worcester County), Maryland. Funds will also be used to market these new value-added products. This working capital will help the farm maximize its economic return by effectively utilizing all components of the milking process and expanding the market for such locally-produced value-added products. This project is expected to create three jobs and save one job. Additional funding for this project includes an applicant contribution of $292,271. Chesapeake Bay Dairy, LLC, better known as Chesapeake Bay Farms, has been a family-owned farm for over 70 years and across four generations. Its a "cow to cone" dairy on Marylands Eastern Shore and is featured on Marylands Ice Cream Trail. USDA Rural Development previously awarded Chesapeake Bay Dairy, LLC a $286,398 value-added producer grant in 2012 to process their own ice cream and a $200,000 value-added producer grant in 2014 for consulting/educational expenses, as well as, packaging/labeling materials needed to produce cheese, milk, and butter.
